source: Desk research of public records and reporting: WV DEP Division of Air Quality permits and notices, WV Air Quality Board, WV PSC dockets, WV Governor / Department of Commerce releases, court records, SEC filings, company statements, and news coverage
scope: every West Virginia data center and crypto-mining site found (proposed, permitted, under construction, operating, stalled or tabled) with what public records say about operator, status, power, water, backup generation, noise and use
disclaimer: Compiled by hand from public sources; not an official list. The state does not publish its High Impact Data Center / microgrid certifications, and HB 2014 keeps certification petitions confidential, so gaps are expected. 'not disclosed' means the developer or agency has not made it public; 'none found' means we searched and found no public record. Each fact cites its source; news and tracker claims are marked as such and can be wrong or out of date. Use labels are evidence-based guesses with a confidence, not findings. Confirm on the linked record. See docs/DATA-CENTERS.md.

sites.name: Monarch Compute Campus
sites.operator: Nscale (Monarch Cloud Campus LLC); formerly Fidelis New Energy / AIPCorp
sites.place: 30 Monarch Way off Ohio River Rd (WV 62), north of Point Pleasant; former Mason County Airport on the WWII West Virginia Ordnance Works
sites.status_detail: Site work since April 2026. High Impact Data Center certification announced 2026-09-03 (Phase 1 ~2 GW, $69.2B claimed). Start-up dates reported from Jan 2027 to early 2028. DEP sediment/dust violation notices May-Aug 2026 and a July 2026 enforcement order.
sites.hb2014: High Impact Data Center (announced 2026-09-03); company calls it the first state-certified AI microgrid, but no Commerce microgrid-district record found

power.mw: 2,160 MW on-site (DEP notice); Microsoft LOI for 1.35 GW
power.supply: off-grid: 864 natural-gas reciprocating engines (2.5 MW each, 12 power nodes); company says Caterpillar G3500 gensets
power.utility: none (off-grid; company says designed to allow future export)
power.gas_supply: 23-mile gas line per a county commissioner; pipeline operator not disclosed (stormwater permit WVR312628 covers 556.5 acres of pipeline work in Putnam and Mason)

water.source: Ohio River 'in limited amounts', no local wells (county commissioner, news)
water.cooling: closed loop: water-cooled chillers plus air-cooled coolers (company / consultant ERM)
water.permits: State waters permits SWP-26-0002 and SWP-26-0003 (wetland/stream fill, 1.78 and 2.98 acres wetland per DEP); no water-withdrawal permit found

air_permits.permits: R14-0042 (major source / PSD; preliminary determination 2026-09-28; written comments to 2026-11-13)
air_permits.backup_generators: 12 diesel emergency generators, 6 diesel fire-water pumps, 18 ULSD tanks (plus the 864 gas engines)

noise.local_rules: HB 2014 bars county noise and light ordinances for certified projects
noise.complaints: yes: neighbors complained of construction noise (news)
noise.measurements: a neighbor reported readings up to 94 dB 'for hours at a time' during construction (news; method not given); no operating noise study disclosed
noise.mitigation: company promises enclosures, mufflers, berms and walls; no dB targets disclosed

use.evidence: Nscale: 'AI training and inference', 'frontier AI workloads'; Microsoft letter of intent for 1.35 GW; Bloomberg reports an Anthropic deal (~460 MW, unconfirmed by the companies)
Microsoft LOI includes 'compute services' and a 'long-term data center lease'
